result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.get_transitivity()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Compute global transitivity (clustering coefficient). ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L9997-L10080){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.get_transitivity() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Transitivity measures the probability that two neighbors of a node are also connected. It's computed as: `transitivity = 3 * (number of triangles) / (number of connected triples)` A connected triple is a path of length 2 (three nodes where at least two edges connect them). Higher transitivity indicates more clustering. Returns `None` if there are no connected triples in the graph. Time complexity: `O(m * d_max)` where `m` is edges and `d_max` is maximum degree. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Optional[float]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Global clustering coefficient between `0.0` and `1.0`, or `None` if undefined. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Perfect triangle has transitivity 1.0: ::: {#da1a9891 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec triangle = ( ec.Graph() .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_edge(source="A", target="B") .add_edge(source="B", target="C") .add_edge(source="C", target="A") ) # Returns 1.0 (all triples are closed) triangle.get_transitivity() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 1.0 ``` ::: ::: Chain graph has transitivity 0.0: ::: {#c94a3083 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} chain = ( ec.Graph() .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_node(label="D") .add_edge(source="A", target="B") .add_edge(source="B", target="C") .add_edge(source="C", target="D") ) # Returns 0.0 (no triangles, only open triples) chain.get_transitivity() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` 0.0 ``` ::: ::: Real-world networks typically have values between 0.1 and 0.5: ::: {#ab050578 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} social_network = ( ec.Graph() .add_node(label="Alice") .add_node(label="Bob") .add_node(label="Charlie") .add_node(label="David") .add_edge(source="Alice", target="Bob") .add_edge(source="Bob", target="Charlie") .add_edge(source="Charlie", target="David") .add_edge(source="David", target="Alice") .add_edge(source="Alice", target="Charlie") # Creates some triangles ) trans = social_network.get_transitivity() # Returns the clustering coefficient (typically 0.1-0.5 for real-world networks) trans ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` 0.75 ``` ::: :::
